title: Protestants deny only free-will or meritorious dispositions
source_text: LV. Quae paulo latius referre visum est, ne adversariis sit obtrectandi locus, ac ne quis dubitare possit, Protestantes non simpliciter negare in peccatore requiri quas-dam dispositiones, sive conditiones praeparatorias, ante justificationem, quocunque modo sumitur, sive Pontificiorum, sive Protestantium sensu: sed ejusmodi solum ad justificationem dispositiones negare, quae vel viribus liberi arbitrii tribuantur, vel concurrere censeantur ad justificationem efficienter, aut meritorie.
pass_a_gloss: Which things it has seemed good to report a little more widely, lest there be room for adversaries to carp, and lest anyone be able to doubt that the Protestants do not simply deny that certain dispositions or preparatory conditions are required in the sinner before justification, in whichever way it is taken, whether in the Papists' or the Protestants' sense: but only deny such dispositions to justification as are either ascribed to the powers of free will, or are thought to concur efficiently or meritoriously toward justification.
pass_b_english: Protestants do not simply deny all preparatory dispositions before justification in either school's sense.
They deny only dispositions ascribed to free will's powers or counted as efficient/meritorious causes.

choices.why: Key lemma for De Justitia densify §1089.
